title: HOP and pipelining both name thingssubmod_i
bug_description:
### 🐛 Describe the bug

Thus stepping on each other's toes.

### HOP
For example:
HOP will translate the following code block:
```
with torch.no_grad():
        expert_counts.scatter_(1, topk_ids, 1)
        tokens_per_expert = expert_counts.sum(dim=0)
```
into:
```
submod_3 = self.submod_1
wrap_with_set_grad_enabled = torch.ops.higher_order.wrap_with_set_grad_enabled(False, submo
d_3, getitem_6);

class submod_1(torch.nn.Module):
         def forward(self, getitem_6: "i64[256, 6]"):
             scatter_: "i64[256, 64]" = torch.ops.aten.scatter_.value(new_zeros, 1, getitem_6, 1);  new_zeros = None
             sum_1: "i64[64]" = torch.ops.aten.sum.dim_IntList(scatter_, [0]);  scatter_ = None
```

### pipelining
pipelining, based on `split_module`, would also name its program partitions as `submod_i` -- hard coded in torch.fx.passes today:
https://github.com/pytorch/pytorch/blob/b48a3d0a38f69fbeeb4375e04ba45389cca12585/torch/fx/passes/split_module.py#L22

### Versions

main
best_code:

        expert_counts.scatter_(1, topk_ids, 1)
        tokens_per_expert = expert_counts.sum(dim=0)
error_description: HOP and pipelining both name things 'submod_i', thus stepping on each other's toes. HOP translates code blocks into submodules named like 'submod_1', and pipelining, based on split_module, also names its program partitions as 'submod_i' (hard coded in torch.fx.passes).
repro_code:

        expert_counts.scatter_(1, topk_ids, 1)
        tokens_per_expert = expert_counts.sum(dim=0)
